key_insight: LLM-based radiology metrics can detect true clinical errors, but they often over-penalize harmless wording changes unless specifically trained to balance discrimination and robustness.
clinical_relevance: A better metric for report evaluation could help identify clinically meaningful mistakes without flagging safe rephrasings, improving trust in generated radiology reports.
method: Tested 8 LLM evaluators on the ReEvalMed benchmark
Compared one-pass vs two-pass metric settings
Trained lightweight interpretable metrics on 4k synthetic report pairs using Qwen3-8B and MedGemma-4B
evidence_signal: Across 8 evaluators, the study found a consistent discrimination bias; the trained metric outperformed 32B-scale medical LLMs and stayed competitive with proprietary models.
watch_item: Two-pass inference increased cost and did not reliably improve overall performance, so deployment should carefully weigh the tradeoff between discrimination and robustness.
paper_title: Beyond Scalar Scores: Exploring LLM-based Metrics for Clinical Significance Evaluation in Radiology Reports
